induction_vs_reference: 1. ELISA analysis of serum from healthy young adults (18–45 yr; MCV4 n=17) at days 0, 7, 30, 180 and 750 post-vaccination showed that MCV4 induced robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C compared to baseline (day 0).

2. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at days 0–14 after vaccination showed that vaccination increased the percentage of total NK cells compared to baseline (day 0).

3. microarray analysis of PBMC from seven Ad5 nAb seronegative individuals during the first week after vaccination, using gene-level analysis of Affymetrix exon microarrays with false-discovery rate (FDR) ≤10% and absolute average log2 fold-change ≥0.5, showed that no significantly differentially expressed genes were detected at 168 h compared to prevaccination.

4. qPCR analysis of RNA from independent YF17D vaccination trials in the Montreal cohort, Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers), and Emory cohort (10 volunteers), at day 0 and day 7 after vaccination, showed that most genes up-regulated in the Montreal cohort also had increased fold-change expression in the Lausanne and Emory cohorts compared to baseline.

5. GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients in a phase 2b trial, on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h thereafter, using Significance Analysis of Microarrays (SAM; Version 3.0) with the day of the third vaccination as baseline, showed that 63 inflammatory-response genes were up-regulated at 24 h after the third vaccination compared to the day of the third vaccination.

6. flow cytometry analysis of cryopreserved PBMC from healthy BCG-vaccinated adults randomized to intradermal or intramuscular MVA85A at weeks 0, 1 and 24 post-vaccination showed that IFNγ, TNFα and IL2 production by mycobacteria-specific CD4+ T cells increased at weeks 1 and 24 compared to baseline (day 0).

7. Microarray analysis of whole blood from healthy adults aged 18 to 64 years after a single intramuscular dose of pneumococcal vaccine, using transcriptional module analysis on whole-genome arrays, showed that the abundance of 70% of transcripts in module M4.11 increased significantly at day 7 compared to prevaccination levels.

8. Flow cytometry analysis of unstimulated PBMC from high and low responders from day of vaccination (day 0) and 1 week later (day 7) showed that the CD4+ CD25+ Foxp3+ Treg population increased in low responders compared to baseline (day 0).

9. Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using additive genotype-effect modeling and delta-Rg2 analysis, showed that multiple loci had genetic effects on expression that were enhanced or only apparent after vaccination compared to baseline.
10. ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed increased influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells compared to baseline (day 0).

11. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (aged 21–30 years; n = 31) and older (aged ≥65 years; n = 36) adults at day 0 and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes increased at days 2 and 7 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

12. ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25 to 40 years; n=5) and elderly adults (60 to 79 years; n=8) at day 7 after Zostavax® vaccination, showed a transient peak of antigen-specific plasmablast cells compared to baseline.

13. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 28, and Day 86 post-vaccination showed that the percentage of CD123+ plasmacytoid dendritic cells increased at Days 7 and 28 compared to baseline (Day 0).
group_difference: 1. GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination before challenge, using high-resolution GSEA with running enrichment score and permutation testing, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was up-regulated in the protected group compared to the nonprotected group.

2. microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male Caucasian volunteers ages 18–40 years immunized on day 0 with the 2008–2009 trivalent influenza vaccine, sampled before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after immunization, using content analysis, showed enrichment of top pathways including the interferon response and antigen presentation pathways among genes upregulated in the high-responder group compared to the low-responder group.

3. ex vivo IFN ELISpot assay analysis of fresh peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy BCG-vaccinated adults randomized to intradermal MVA85A (n = 12) or intramuscular MVA85A (n = 12) at screening and 1, 2, 4, 12 and 24 weeks post-vaccination showed no significant difference in Ag85A-specific IFN responses between the intradermal and intramuscular groups compared to each other.

4. microarray analysis of PBMC from subjects with high and low CD8+ T-cell response groups after MRKAd5/HIV, using direct comparison of MRKAd5-responsive modules, showed that none of the MRKAd5-responsive modules differed significantly between the groups.

5. Microarray analysis of blood from an independent patient cohort (n = 6 subjects per group) collected at hours -168, 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48 following vaccine or saline administration, using circular-plot comparison of lists of genes differentially expressed at nine consecutive post-vaccine time points with in vitro blood-stimulation gene-expression profiles after 6 hr stimulation, showed that the gene lists obtained for the saline group were only sparsely connected compared to the vaccine groups.

6. IFN-γ ELISpot analysis of splenocytes from mice vaccinated intradermally with MVA85A and culled 7 days later showed no significant difference in mean antigen 85A responses after co-administration of anti-TLR2 compared to MVA85A alone or MVA85A with isotype control.

7. Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in the discovery and validation cohorts, obtained on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination on day 0, using extended causal modeling with independent-versus-reactive and independent-versus-causal hypothesis tests, showed that patterns in the 137 eQTL SNP-transcript pairs from the 20 loci with the strongest evidence of genetic variation influencing the immune response to the vaccine trended toward the causal model compared to the reactive model.

8. Serum bactericidal assay analysis of serum from 30 healthy young adults (18–45 years of age) vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) over day 750 post-vaccination showed no difference in the proportion with an SBA titer of 1:8 or higher between MPSV4 vaccinees and MCV4 vaccinees compared to MCV4 vaccinees.

9. Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, 7, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that predictive cell populations remained able to separate high and low adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) responders compared to each other over time.

10. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (aged 21–30 years; n = 31) and older (aged ≥65 years; n = 36) adults at day 0 and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-10 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was higher in older subjects than in young subjects at all time points compared to young subjects.

11. Plaque assay analysis of lungs from groups of C57BL/6 mice mock infected or infected with 4×10^4 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged with 10^6 EID50 of IAV ×31 i.n. 5 weeks later, showed reduced influenza viral titers in IAV+ MCMV+ mice compared to IAV+ MCMV− mice at day 7 after IAV infection.

12. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects after TIV vaccination at days 0–14, using area-under-the-curve comparison by t test, showed that total NK-cell proportions within all PBMCs were higher in elderly subjects compared to young subjects throughout the study duration (days 0–14).

13. microarray analysis of PAXgene blood samples from the EM131 training set (n=95) before HBV vaccination, using LIMMA with adjusted P≤0.05, showed no significantly differentially expressed transcript between HBV vaccine responders and poor-responders.
extremum: 1. ELISA analysis of serum from healthy young adults (18–45 yr; MCV4 n=17) at days 0, 7, 30, 180 and 750 post-vaccination showed that the polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody response against serogroups A and C peaked at day 30 compared to days 0, 7, 180 and 750.

2. microarray analysis of PBMC from seven Ad5 nAb seronegative individuals during the first week after vaccination, using gene-level analysis of Affymetrix exon microarrays with false-discovery rate (FDR) ≤10% and absolute average log2 fold-change ≥0.5, showed that responses to MRKAd5/HIV peaked at 24 h compared to prevaccination across the candidate set of prevaccination, 24 h, 72 h, and 168 h postvaccination.

3. GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination before challenge, using high-resolution GSEA with permutation testing and multiple-test correction, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was the only gene set with both a significant nominal P value and an FDR less than 0.25 compared to the gene sets tested.

4. Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort on day 0 and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination, using heat map representation and principal component analysis, showed that gene expression modulation was greatest at days 3 and 7 among the measured post-vaccination timepoints.

5. ex vivo IFN ELISpot assay analysis of fresh peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy BCG-vaccinated adults randomized to intradermal or intramuscular MVA85A (n = 12 per group) at screening and 1, 2, 4, 12 and 24 weeks post-vaccination showed that Ag85A-specific IFN responses peaked at day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

6. Microarray analysis of whole blood from first-cohort volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group; 162 samples in total) across the study time points, using linear mixed models with contrasts versus baseline and false discovery rate adjustment, showed that the number of responsive genes was largest in the pneumococcal vaccine group compared to the influenza vaccine and saline control groups.

7. Illumina microarray analysis of PBMC from 24 BCG-primed healthy adults from the UK vaccinated with MVA85A at day 0, day 2 and day 7 post-vaccination showed that CXCL10 (IP-10) had the greatest change in gene expression on day 2 compared to baseline (day 0).

8. Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that B-cell subsets including ID103 and ID91 had some of the highest inter-subject variation among measured cell populations compared to other cell populations.

9. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (aged 21–30 years; n = 31) and older (aged ≥65 years; n = 36) adults at day 0 and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-10 production in classical CD14+CD16− monocytes increased progressively to highest levels at day 28 compared to days 0, 2, and 7.

10. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from elderly subjects after TIV vaccination on day 3, using CD69 staining with geometric mean fluorescence intensity (MFI), showed that CD69 expression in all three NK-cell subsets was highest on day 3 among the measured post-vaccination time points.

11. ELISA analysis of serum samples from 174 healthy adults in the EM131 cohort before and after vaccination, showed that anti-HBsAg had the lowest percentage of study participants above the protective antibody threshold compared to anti-Tetanus toxin, anti-Diphtheria toxin, and anti-Cholera toxin.

12. ELISPOT analysis of cryopreserved PBMCs from a subset of HLA-A2+ individuals (n=13) sampled at baseline and post-vaccination timepoints after Zostavax® vaccination, showed that subject ZV118 had the highest CD8+ response to the vaccine peptides among the individuals assessed.

13. Affymetrix arrays analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy, YFV seronegative volunteers at 4 h and Days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14, 28, 84 and 168 post-vaccination showed that JUP, STAT1, and EIF2AK2 expression peaked on Days 5 and 7 compared to Hour 4, Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 14, and Day 28.
response_difference: 1. Microarray analysis of PBMCs from young (<65 years) and elderly (≥65 years) vaccinees in the 2010 season at days 1, 3, 7, and 14 after vaccination, using differential expression analysis, showed that the young exhibited a greater number of both up- and downregulated genes on day 1 after vaccination (day 1) compared to the elderly.

2. Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from young vaccinated subjects in the first study year (20-30 years old), using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that the antibody response was higher in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− subjects.

3. ELISA analysis of serum from 30 healthy young adults (18–45 years of age) vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) over days 0, 7, 30, 180 and 750 post-vaccination showed that the magnitude of the polysaccharide-specific IgG response was greater in MPSV4 vaccinees compared to MCV4 vaccinees.

4. Luminex analysis of serum from vaccinated subjects at prevaccination and 24 h, using serum IP-10/CXCL10 concentrations contrasted between Ad5 nAb ≤200 and Ad5 nAb >200 individuals with *P < 0.05 after Hochberg adjustment, showed that serum IP-10/CXCL10 induction was attenuated in Ad5 nAb >200 subjects compared to Ad5 nAb ≤200 subjects.

5. Flow cytometry analysis of whole blood from healthy adults aged 18 to 64 years after a single intramuscular dose of seasonal influenza vaccine, pneumococcal vaccine, or saline control, using polychromatic multi-parameter flow cytometry with abundance of plasmablasts plotted on a graph, showed that plasmablast and/or plasma cell expansion was greater after pneumococcal vaccination than after influenza vaccination compared to prevaccination levels.

6. ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25 to 40 years; n=16) and elderly adults (60 to 79 years; n=21) sampled at baseline (day 0) and day 28 after Zostavax® vaccination, showed that the younger group had a greater increase of VZV-specific antibody after vaccination compared to the elderly group.
